details: Question for the owner. How it works: relay sync rewrites only the files named in projects.toml; the 10 project files
were written by it until today and now stop changing. Live example: ~/alix/CLAUDE.local.md loads OpenSpec and quality-gate
full texts, and the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md already lists those rules as "read when they apply", so the projects keep
their rules either way; only future rule edits stop reaching their full text.
Options: (a) leave them frozen (recommended now: nothing breaks, the portable-tool change decides where per-project
settings live); (b) rewrite the header so the file reads as the project's own; (c) delete them and rely on the global list.
The brief marks deleting them as not decided, so this change correctly left them. Size: 5 agent minutes for (b) or (c).
evidence: head -3 ~/alix/CLAUDE.local.md -> "<!-- Generated by relay (relay sync). Edit rules/ and profiles/active.toml, not this file. -->"
bin/relay sync --dry -> only global, relay, agents
failing_case: ~/alix/CLAUDE.local.md starts "Generated by relay (relay sync). Edit rules/ and profiles/active.toml, not this file."
After this change, editing rules/openspec.md and running relay sync leaves it as it is: the project keeps the old
rule text forever, and its header points the reader at a source that no longer reaches it. If a rule is renamed
(the queued taste -> principles change), its "Full text: ~/relay/rules/<x>.md" lines can point at a missing file.
fix_hint: None in this change; the owner's answer goes to the portable-tool queue item.
pass_cases: - The owner picks one: (a) leave the files frozen as they are (today's brief), (b) strip relay's header so they read as the project's own text, (c) remove the files so the projects get only the global list.
- Whatever the pick, docs say what happens to a project's CLAUDE.local.md once it leaves projects.toml.
findings.summary: the 10 projects keep a CLAUDE.local.md that says it is generated by relay sync, but sync no longer writes it
